entire_proof_units.statement: Exact continuous-PC criterion for complete rational branches meeting only at a common rational point, with no direct-sum assumption.
entire_proof_units.proof:
Translate the common rational point to zero. Let Q_1,...,Q_r be complete rational d-planes, d>=1, with Q_i intersect Q_j={0} for i!=j. Their sum may be dependent. Give the union its induced finite rational complex and a positive balanced top cycle sum_i c_i[Q_i], c_i>0 REAL. A continuous function f on the union is printed-PC if and only if (i) every restriction f_i to Q_i is ordinary convex, (ii) every f_i(0) is the same REAL number a, and (iii) there exists one ambient REAL linear form p with f_i(x)>=a+p(x) for every i and x in Q_i.
Here is necessity of (i), including the common point. On a complete branch a sufficiently small neighborhood of any center meets only cells incident to its center face. Rational centers in that rational face and rational opposite displacements satisfying the finite incident-cone constraints are dense in the feasible pairs. The printed two-endpoint relation with weights1/2 gives the local midpoint inequality, and continuity passes it to arbitrary real pairs near that center. At zero the inherited common face is {0}; branch endpoints sufficiently near zero lie in incident branch cells, so the same opposite-pair argument applies. Continuous midpoint convexity gives local convexity by dyadic subdivision. Restriction to any compact line segment and a finite cover by these neighborhoods makes the secant slopes nondecreasing across the cover, hence gives ordinary convexity on the whole complete branch. This uses the inherited incident cells and rational refinements, not permission to coarsen them. Condition(ii) follows from single-valuedness and continuity. Necessity of(iii) is proved in T2.
For sufficiency, a printed center x!=0 lies on a unique branch. Every cell incident to its center face is contained in that branch: a positive-dimensional convex cell cannot pass between two planes whose intersection is only zero without containing a segment outside their union. Thus its printed relation is ordinary branch Jensen. At zero, for any finite relation with endpoints x_j, coefficients alpha_j>=0, sum alpha_j=1 and sum alpha_j x_j=0, the shared minorant gives sum alpha_j f(x_j)>=a+p(sum alpha_j x_j)=a. This works for all actual REAL relation weights, all rational endpoints and every rational refinement. Pairwise-zero intersection is essential in the nonzero-center part. No ambient-convexity of the whole function is asserted.

entire_proof_units.statement: The origin printed relations force a common ambient supporting form, by compact finite-dimensional separation and rational zero-relation approximation.
entire_proof_units.proof:
For each finite continuous convex f_i on the complete vector space Q_i, its subdifferential K_i at zero is nonempty, compact and convex. Equivalently define the finite continuous sublinear directional derivative h_i(v)=lim_{t downarrow0}(f_i(tv)-a)/t and let K_i={ell in Q_i*:ell(v)<=h_i(v) for all v}. Local Lipschitzness bounds K_i. Finite-dimensional supporting-hyperplane separation, or extension of a linear form dominated by h_i, gives nonemptiness and h_i(v)=max_{ell in K_i}ell(v). These are ordinary finite convex facts; the existence of any original envelope or raw measure is not assumed. The derivative limit exists by monotonicity of convex secants; its support representation also proves its continuity.
Put K=product_i K_i, a compact convex subset of product_i Q_i*. Let S be the image of the ambient restriction map p -> (p|Q_i)_i, a CLOSED linear subspace. If K and S were disjoint, minimize the squared norm of the orthogonal projection of K to S-perp. Compactness gives a minimizer k0 with q=projection(k0)!=0. The first variation of this convex quadratic along the segment from k0 to k in K gives <q,k> >= |q|^2 for every k in K. Hence z=-q annihilates S and max_{k in K}<z,k><0. Identify the dual of product_i Q_i* with tuples v_i in Q_i. Annihilating S means sum_i v_i=0 as an AMBIENT vector, and the strict inequality is sum_i h_i(v_i)<0.
Because the branch embeddings have rational matrices, the kernel { (v_i):sum_i v_i=0 } has a rational basis by Gaussian elimination. Approximate this tuple inside its kernel by rational tuples. Continuity of the h_i preserves the strict negative sum. Discard any zero vectors. Choose one sufficiently small positive RATIONAL t. Every endpoint tv_i is rational and lies in a cell incident to the origin. Directional differentiability along this fixed finite tuple yields sum_i [f_i(tv_i)-a]=t sum_i h_i(v_i)+o(t)<0. With equal coefficients1/m, where m is the number of remaining endpoints, these points have exact barycenter zero and violate the printed origin inequality. This is a genuine legal finite rational PCC, not an irrational relation substituted into the definition. Contradiction proves K intersects S. Its preimage p satisfies f_i(x)>=a+p(x) on every complete branch, establishing T1(iii). This argument permits arbitrary linear dependencies among the branches; it never groups their means as if their sum were direct.

entire_proof_units.statement: Full-affine global approximation from ABOVE with exact value at a prescribed rational point, for arbitrary ACTUAL REAL positive-growth PA reference on rational geometry.
entire_proof_units.proof:
Work first on a single saturated rational affine d-space, translated so the prescribed rational point is zero. Let gamma be the ACTUAL continuous convex finite REAL PA reference on a finite rational carrier and gamma>=b|x|-B with b>0. Let f be any continuous convex function with |f-gamma|<=C. Write gamma=max_j(a_j.x+b_j) with actual REAL gradients and set h(x)=max_j a_j.x and Delta=conv{a_j}. Then |f-h| is bounded on the WHOLE space; Delta is a compact full-dimensional polytope, possibly with irrational vertices.
The recession cones of the finite rational carrying cells cover the whole vector space. To see coverage without an assumption on arbitrary carriers, on a ray tv choose an unbounded subsequence contained in one cell among the finitely many cells; its recession cone contains v. Positive growth makes every carrying cell pointed: a lineality direction would have opposite gamma recession slopes, which cannot both be strictly positive. On each recession cone, h equals the linear part of that cell. Choose finite rational ray generators r for all these cones. The cone E_h=epi(h) is EXACTLY generated by (r,h(r)) and the upward vertical ray: on each cone the graph height is linear, so its rational conic spatial decomposition lifts with equality. All heights may be REAL; spatial generators are rational. These are genuine finite polyhedral data, not a claim of a rational epigraph in d+1 coordinates.
The conjugate f*(p)=sup_x(p.x-f(x)) is finite on Delta, infinite outside Delta, convex and lower semicontinuous. On Delta, p.x<=h(x) gives a uniform upper bound and x=0 a finite lower bound. Outside Delta, strict separation gives a direction along which the supremum diverges. A finite lower-semicontinuous convex function g on a compact polytope is continuous EVEN ON ITS BOUNDARY: its values are bounded above by the largest vertex value. At a point x, choose a radius smaller than the finitely many positive inactive-inequality slacks divided by their covector norms. For nearby y in the polytope extend the ray xy to that radius to obtain z still in the polytope; active inequalities remain valid and inactive ones remain valid by the slack choice. Write y=(1-t)x+t z with t tending to zero. Convexity gives limsup g(y)<=g(x), and lower semicontinuity gives the reverse liminf. Degenerate affine spans are treated in their own space. This proves whole-polytope continuity without an unsupported boundary regularity assertion.
Since f is continuous, the defining supremum for f* can be taken over rational spatial x. For any eta>0, choose at each p in Delta a rational x giving p.x-f(x)>f*(p)-eta/2. Continuity of f* makes this inequality with error eta valid on a neighborhood of p. Compactness selects FINITELY many such rational samples A; append0. Then g_A(p)=max_{x in A}(p.x-f(x)) satisfies f*(p)-eta<=g_A(p)<=f*(p) on ALL Delta. Let
 E_A=conv{(x,f(x)):x in A}+E_h.
This is closed: its first summand is compact and the second a closed finitely generated polyhedral cone. It is a finite REAL polyhedron with rational SPATIAL generators. Its projection is the whole vector space and it is upward closed. It is contained in epi(f). Indeed convexity and the bound relative to h imply f(x+v)<=f(x)+h(v): otherwise convex secants along x+tv would force a recession slope greater than h(v), contradicting |f-h| bounded. Apply this inequality to convex combinations of the samples and each cone generator. Thus E_A=epi(F_A) for a finite convex function F_A>=f; it also contains the sample(0,a), so F_A(0)=f(0)=a EXACTLY.
Its conjugate is g_A on Delta and infinity outside, by the compact-hull support formula and the polar inequalities of E_h. The elementary biconjugate identity for finite continuous convex functions follows from separating a point below their closed epigraph; equivalently from their supporting affine minorants. Consequently conjugating the uniform inequalities on Delta gives f<=F_A<=f+eta on the WHOLE affine space. This is global uniform approximation, not merely compact convergence.
Every lower face of E_A has its height as a single affine function of the spatial coordinate. It is generated by subsets of the finitely many lifted sample vertices and cone rays, excluding the vertical ray. Its spatial projection is therefore the convex hull of rational sample positions plus the cone of rational ray positions. This is a RATIONAL polyhedron despite irrational heights. The projection is injective on the lower graph, so projected face intersections and shared-face incidences are preserved. There are finitely many lower faces; they give a finite rational spatial complex on which F_A is continuous REAL PA. Its convexity makes it printed-PC; F_A is bounded relative to the ACTUAL unchanged gamma. No maximum wall with irrational spatial position is declared primitive. This proves genuine finite primitive-sector approximants BEFORE assigning any MA to f. The construction includes the exact contact sample at any prescribed rational point after rational translation, and it uses neither coefficient rounding nor unbounded recession perturbation.

entire_proof_units.statement: GLOBAL decreasing same-reference regularization on arbitrary dependent branches with pairwise point intersections.
entire_proof_units.proof:
Let f be continuous printed-PC on X and |f-gamma|<=C for the ACTUAL admitted reference. T1 gives convex branch restrictions with common origin value a and one supporting ambient REAL linear form p. Apply the entire T3 proof to each complete branch and actual gamma_i, choosing global error eta_n=2^-n and including the rational origin among its samples. This gives finite rational-geometry REAL PA convex F_{i,n} with f_i<=F_{i,n}<=f_i+eta_n and EXACT origin value a. In particular F_{i,n}>=a+p on every branch: the shared supporting form is retained automatically by approximation from ABOVE. This retention is the step that arbitrary two-sided approximants and simple origin-value alignment would not supply on dependent branches.
Refine each finite rational carrier to contain zero as a face. The finite branch carriers join into a rational complex since every distinct pair intersects only at the same rational point. The F_{i,n} glue into F_n, which is continuous and printed-PC by T1. Its global error is at most eta_n. Put G_n=F_n+4eta_n. Its origin value is the common a+4eta_n, and a+4eta_n+p is a shared branch minorant, so G_n is still printed-PC. On ALL X,
 4eta_n<=G_n-f<=5eta_n,
 whereas G_{n+1}-f<=2.5eta_n<4eta_n<=G_n-f.
Thus G_n decreases everywhere to f, globally uniformly, through genuine finite REAL PA PC functions on rational geometry boundedly relative to the SAME ACTUAL gamma. The relative bound is uniform in n. This is the actual global real completion; the proof does not change its topology or define an operator by local limits. No direct-sum independence, branchwise zero means, rational shared height, rational reference gradients, or separability of f is assumed.

entire_proof_units.statement: All bounded continuous-obstacle envelope regularity, with its genuine operator antecedent, in this larger geometric sector.
entire_proof_units.proof: For ANY u in C_b(X), including arbitrary coupled or non-PA obstacles, the entire accepted R230 result with all clarifications identifies its ACTUAL unrestricted envelope f=P_gamma(u) as continuous printed-PC and gamma-||u||<=f<=gamma+||u||. Apply T4 to THIS actual envelope. Its genuine globally decreasing real-PA regularization is proved before applying the entire S272 genuine-completion theorem. Only then is MA_raw(f) assigned as its genuine positive finite Radon measure with the same actual raw mass. The finite convex probabilities and support constructions in T2/T3 are never called MA. This proves universal real envelope-domain regularity on finite globally embedded arrangements of complete equal-dimensional rational planes all meeting pairwise only at one rational point. Arbitrary positive REAL constant branch weights are allowed; they do not alter the printed-PC criterion or the approximation. This is a specified-sector theorem, not the complete original P05.1 classification.

entire_proof_units.statement: For at least two such branches there is a genuine finite-PA strictly negative contact example at EVERY admitted actual reference.
entire_proof_units.proof:
Choose Q_1 and a nonzero rational line L in Q_2. Their intersection is zero. Extend the saturated dual coordinates on Q_1 to rational ambient forms ell_1,...,ell_d vanishing on L; this is possible by solving rational linear equations on Q_1+L and extending to the ambient space. There is no claim that these forms vanish on every OTHER branch. Set h=sum_j |ell_j|. It is a rational homogeneous ambient convex PA germ and thus printed-PC on X, and h vanishes on both directions of L, giving a legal flat origin PCC. Its raw atom on Q_1 is c_1 2^d d!: each distinct-factor ordered product uses successive saturated coordinate kernels and gives2^d delta0; repeated factors vanish after commuting a repeated factor next to its own first derivative. There are d! distinct orders.
More generally on a branch Q_i with a saturated basis and restriction matrix A_i of the ell_j, the same primitive recursion gives2^d |det A_i| delta0, with zero for a singular matrix. For a nonsingular rational matrix clear denominators, choose saturated kernel bases successively by the Euclidean algorithm, and track the primitive normal evaluation as the absolute ratio of consecutive minors; these ratios telescope to |det A_i|. Multilinear expansion has d! distinct orders; no factorial is appended to an independently normalized operator. Equivalently this is the whole S272 strictly saturated distinct-factor calculation specialized to the stated restriction matrices. All c_i are positive, so the full atom is
 m=2^d d! sum_i c_i |det A_i| >= 2^d d! c_1 >0,
 since A_1 is the identity. The determinants and primitive recursions use the actual lattice on each branch, not Euclidean nonsaturated normal lengths.
The whole accepted S272 flat-jet theorem with every clarification realizes this rational germ in a genuine finite relative REAL PA function F for the SAME actual gamma, inserting the same scaled germ in each reference summand. The origin atom is delta^d m>0 and the flat relation is retained. Its granted roof construction supplies a bounded continuous REAL PA obstacle u=F-gamma+(R-rho)_+ with actual envelope F and raw contact integral EXACTLY -R delta^d m<0. The function, reference and operator antecedents are all genuinely finite PA before the integral. Thus universal all-C_b real regularity from T5 coexists with contact failure; it is not a sufficient contact criterion. One-branch full contact is the separately investigated full-affine sector, not a new grant imported here.

entire_proof_units.statement: An exact dependent three-plane example shows why common origin values alone do not suffice.
entire_proof_units.proof:
In rational R4 let Q_1={(x,y,0,0)}, Q_2={(0,0,z,w)}, and Q_3={(t,s,t,s)}. Their pairwise intersections are zero, but their threefold sum is not direct. Use the positive balanced cycle with weight1 on each plane. Define the ACTUAL reference by gamma_1=|x|+|y|, gamma_2=|z|+|w| and gamma_3=|t|+|s|. Its restrictions are convex, share value0, and admit the ambient supporting form0, so T1 proves printed-PC; it has strictly positive growth on the whole union.
The continuous finite rational PA function with restrictions f_1=|x-1|+|y|-1, f_2=|z-1|+|w|-1 and f_3=|t|+|s| has common origin value0, convex branch restrictions, and -2<=f-gamma<=0. Nevertheless at rational endpoints a=(1/2,0,0,0), b=(0,0,1/2,0), c=(-1/2,0,-1/2,0) its values are -1/2,-1/2,+1/2. Their equal-weight barycenter is EXACTLY0, and the average value is -1/6<0=f(0). The endpoint cells are incident to the origin after the rational quadrant/carrier refinement; this is a legal printed PCC. Thus f is not PC. This is not an envelope counterexample or an operator-domain failure: it verifies exactly the extra supporting-form condition required by T1. On Q_1 any supporting form at0 has x coefficient-1, and on Q_2 it has z coefficient-1; its restriction to Q_3 would have t coefficient-2, outside the subgradient interval[-1,1] of |t|. There is no common supporting ambient form. The T4 above-touching construction explicitly retains that form for the genuine PC inputs to which the theorem applies.

steps.statement: Exact continuous-PC criterion with a separate common supporting form at every finite intersection point.
steps.proof:
Let X be the finite union of distinct complete rational affine d-planes Q_i, d>=1, every pair having either EMPTY intersection or ONE POINT. There may be several intersection points, and more than two branches may meet at any one of them. Rational Gaussian elimination finds every nonempty intersection point as a rational point. Let V be this finite set and I(v)={i:v in Q_i}. Every plane has the given positive REAL constant weight; their sum is an effective balanced cycle.
A continuous function f on X is printed-PC precisely when each f_i is ordinary convex, the branch values agree at every v in V, and for each v there is one ambient REAL linear form p_v such that f_i(x)>=f(v)+p_v(x-v) for EVERY i in I(v) and x in Q_i. This does not require the supporting form to be the same at different points.
Necessity of branch convexity is the entire inherited-cell rational-midpoint/segment argument T1. At an intersection v, translate all incident branches by v. Their tangent planes have pairwise zero intersections because their original complete affine planes intersect only at v. Every nonincident plane is closed and has positive distance from v; there are finitely many, so a small ball misses all of them. Thus all sufficiently small printed splits constructed in T2 belong to the actual incident star at v. The ENTIRE T2 compact product-subgradient/closed restriction-subspace separation and rational-kernel zero-relation proof supplies a common p_v. Its support inequality is global on each complete convex branch, not merely local at v. Agreements follow from single-valuedness.
For sufficiency, a center outside V is on a unique branch and all cells incident to its center face lie on that branch, so branch Jensen applies. A center v in V has every endpoint cell in an incident branch, and its endpoints obey f(x_j)>=f(v)+p_v(x_j-v). Summing the finite relation gives the origin inequality without grouping branch means. This argument holds on every rational refinement, not only a convenient selected fan. At an intersection the common face is the rational vertex v. The branchwise support is enough even for incident endpoint cells extending far beyond the small ball. No ambient-convexity conclusion on the entire union is used.

steps.statement: The primal approximation retains EXACT values at every point of any prescribed finite rational set.
steps.proof: In the entire full-affine T3 proof, append a FINITE rational set B to the finite rational sample set A chosen by the dual compactness argument. Including extra samples still gives f*-eta<=g_A<=f* on the whole actual recession polytope; every sample term lies below f*. The resulting finite epigraph hull lies inside epi(f) and includes EVERY (b,f(b)), b in B. Therefore its genuine real PA lower boundary obeys f<=F_A<=f+eta globally AND F_A(b)=f(b) EXACTLY at every b. Arbitrary REAL sample heights introduce no irrational spatial wall: the whole T3 lower-face projection argument still gives rational spatial polyhedra. The ACTUAL reference and recession cone remain unchanged. No uniform error, above-approximation or exact-touch property is lost by appending finitely many points. This is the crucial strengthening needed for several intersections; it does not assert exact agreement on a positive-dimensional overlap or on an infinite contact set.

steps.statement: GLOBAL decreasing same-reference regularization of every continuous-PC endpoint, and hence every C_b actual envelope, on finite point-intersection arrangements.
steps.proof:
Let f be continuous printed-PC on X with |f-gamma|<=C for the ACTUAL admitted REAL PA positive-growth reference. By C1 each f_i is convex and the finitely many support forms p_v exist. On each complete branch choose its saturated rational coordinates and an arbitrary rational affine origin. Apply the ENTIRE T3 construction, using C2 to append ALL the finitely many points V intersect Q_i as exact samples, and global error eta_n=2^-n. This gives genuine finite rational-geometry REAL PA convex F_{i,n} with f_i<=F_{i,n}<=f_i+eta_n and exact shared values f(v) at every incident v. Approximation from ABOVE retains every supporting minorant f(v)+p_v(x-v) on each incident branch.
Refine each branch's finite rational carrier by finitely many rational hyperplanes through its intersection points, so all those points are vertices. Union of the branch complexes is a finite rational complex: distinct-branch cells can meet only at one of those vertices, which is then a common face. The approximants glue continuously and satisfy the complete C1 PC criterion at all centers. There are only finitely many branches, so their maximum global error is at most eta_n. Put G_n=F_n+4eta_n on X; all vertex values shift by the SAME constant and every supporting minorant shifts by that constant. Thus G_n is actual PC REAL PA on rational geometry, boundedly relative to the SAME actual gamma. The whole T4 estimate gives 4eta_n<=G_n-f<=5eta_n and G_{n+1}-f<=2.5eta_n<4eta_n, so the sequence decreases everywhere to f, globally uniformly.
For an arbitrary u in C_b(X), the whole R230 grant with every clarification gives the ACTUAL unrestricted envelope f=P_gamma(u) continuous-PC and |f-gamma|<=||u||. The preceding construction proves its genuine GLOBAL completion membership BEFORE the whole S272 raw mixed completion assigns a finite positive Radon MA measure and common raw mass. The obstacle may be non-PA, coupled and nonseparable; no approximation of u in global C_b norm is assumed. This proves universal real envelope-domain regularity throughout this specified finite point-intersection arrangement sector. The proof includes disjoint arrangements and one branch. Positive REAL cycle weights are retained and do not influence the gluing construction.

steps.statement: Scope, contact witnesses and residual originals.
steps.proof:
Whenever two branches in this arrangement meet, choose a rational meeting point v, a complete incident branch Q_1-v, and a rational line in another incident branch transverse to Q_1-v. The entire T6 rational dual-form and saturated determinant argument applies to the tangent sum at v, which contains precisely the complete planes through v. Its positive residual is explicitly effective and balanced. The whole S272 actual-reference jet realization and roof theorem yield a genuine finite relative REAL PA negative-contact witness at the SAME actual gamma. Thus the all-C_b regularity theorem here does not imply contact at a crossing. No contact sufficiency claim for the disjoint case is imported as a new grant from the active/unreviewed282 paper; its independent full-affine proof remains a separate mathematical result.
This new theorem covers FINITELY many COMPLETE rational affine d-planes with pairwise intersections empty or zero-dimensional, including distinct rational points, arbitrary dependencies and arbitrary positive REAL weights. It does not cover positive-dimensional overlaps or arbitrary polyhedral singular supports, curved charts or abstract glued compact spaces. The exact-touch construction uses a FINITE sample set and supplies no approximation preserving values on an entire affine intersection. Continuous printed-PC is not claimed globally ambient convex. Literal PA_Z remains separate, with the accepted S262 noncompact obstruction in its own exact domain; no excluded endpoint receives a measure. Original P05.1/P05.2 full necessary-and-sufficient classifications remain OPEN. The WHOLE old287 proof is included as UNREVIEWED working DATA rather than a sixth grant; every used T1/T2/T3/T4/T6 argument must be independently reconstructed in a future whole review.
